question: What is USMA?
answer: USMA (Unified Scholarship Mobile Application) is a single-window mobile platform developed for MoTA (Ministry of Tribal Affairs) Scheduled Tribe students to discover, apply, track, and manage all 5 official scholarship schemes: Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class Education, National Fellowship (NFST), and National Overseas Scholarship (NOS).

question: Which official scholarship schemes are covered under MoTA?
answer:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs (tribal.nic.in) implements 5 major schemes:
1. Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST Students (Class 9 & 10)
2. Post-Matric Scholarship for ST Students (Class 11 to Ph.D)
3. National Scholarship Scheme (Top Class Education in 265 Premier Institutes)
4. National Fellowship for ST Students (NFST for M.Phil & Ph.D)
5. National Overseas Scholarship (NOS for Master's/Ph.D abroad)

question: What are the rules and financial rates for Pre-Matric ST Scholarship?
answer:
• Target: ST Students in Classes IX & X.
• Family Income Limit: Up to ₹2.50 Lakhs per annum.
• Rates: ₹225/month for Day Scholars & ₹525/month for Hostellers (for 10 months/year).
• Fund Sharing: 75:25 (Centre:State), 90:10 for North-East & Hilly States (J&K, HP, UK), and 100% for UTs without legislature.
• Portal: https://dbttribal.gov.in/

question: What are the features of Post-Matric Scholarship for ST Students (PMS-ST)?
answer:
• Target: ST Students pursuing Class XI, XII, ITI, Diploma, Graduation, Post-Graduation, or Ph.D.
• Family Income Limit: Up to ₹2.50 Lakhs per annum.
• Benefits: 1) Full non-refundable compulsory fees charged by institution. 2) Maintenance allowance ranging from ₹230 to ₹1,200 per month.
• Fund Sharing: 75:25 (Centre:State), 90:10 (NE/Hilly States), 100% (UTs).
• Portal: https://dbttribal.gov.in/

question: What is the National Scholarship Scheme for Top Class Education?
answer:
• Target: ST Students admitted to 265 notified premier institutes (IITs, NITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NLUs, etc.).
• Family Income Limit: Up to ₹6.00 Lakhs per annum.
• Coverage: Full tuition fees + living allowance (₹3,000/month) + books & stationery allowance (₹5,000/year) + one-time computer assistance (₹45,000).
• Portal: https://scholarships.gov.in (NSP)

question: What are the highlights of National Fellowship for ST Students (NFST)?
answer:
• Target: ST Students pursuing full-time M.Phil & Ph.D degrees in UGC recognized universities & institutes of national importance.
• Annual Slots: 750 fresh fellowships awarded every year on Master's merit.
• Special Preference: Given to female scholars, Divyangjan (PwD), and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
• Family Income Limit: Up to ₹6.00 Lakhs per annum.
• Fellowship Amount: M.Phil @ ₹25,000/month, Ph.D @ ₹28,000/month + HRA + Contingency.
• Portal: https://fellowship.tribal.gov.in/

question: What is National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) for ST Students?
answer:
• Target: Meritorious ST students pursuing Master's, Ph.D, and Post-Doctoral research in foreign universities.
• Awards: 20 slots/year (17 STs + 3 PVTGs).
• Family Income Limit: Up to ₹6.00 Lakhs per annum.
• Financial Assistance: Full tuition fees + Annual Maintenance Allowance of USD 15,400 + Contingency Allowance USD 1,532 + Visa fees + Medical Insurance + Air passage expenses.
• Portal: https://overseas.tribal.gov.in/

question: How do I link my existing NSP or state portal application?
answer: Go to the Dashboard and tap 'Link Application'. Select your source portal (NSP, SFMP, or NOS), choose the scheme, and enter your application reference ID. USMA will fetch and display your live application status.

question: What documents are mandatory for MoTA scholarship application?
answer:
Mandatory documents:
1. ST Community Certificate (issued by Tehsildar / SDO / Tehsildar)
2. Valid Income Certificate for current financial year
3. Aadhaar Card (linked to mobile & NPCI bank account)
4. Previous Year Academic Marksheet & Passing Certificate
5. Admission Fee Receipt & Bonafide Student Certificate
6. Bank Passbook page (showing Account No. & IFSC)

question: What does 'deficiency raised' mean and how to fix it?
answer:
Deficiency raised means the verification officer (Institute or State Nodal Officer) found an error — like a blurred marksheet or invalid income certificate.
Fix: Open 'Applications', check officer comments, upload the revised document in 'Document Vault', and resubmit before the deadline.

question: Can I hold two government scholarships at the same time?
answer: No. As per Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) guidelines, a student can avail only ONE government scholarship or fellowship at any given time. If you apply for multiple schemes, your application will be flagged during central verification.

question: What is DBT and why is Aadhaar-NPCI seeding mandatory?
answer:
DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) sends scholarship funds directly into your bank account through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
Aadhaar seeding with NPCI is mandatory because payments are disbursed using Aadhaar-based Mapper routing to prevent middleman leakages.

question: How does DigiLocker integration work with USMA?
answer: DigiLocker is a secure Government of India digital document repository. In USMA, you can link your DigiLocker account to automatically fetch pre-verified ST certificates, Aadhaar cards, and Class 10/12 marksheets without manual scanning.

question: Can I use USMA offline?
answer: Yes! USMA includes local offline caching powered by Hive. You can check your application timeline, view saved documents, and access scholarship criteria without an active internet connection.
